345733.title: Discrete Hurewicz conjecture for higher homotopy groups of graphs
345733.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $A_k(G)$ denote its $k$th discrete homotopy group, and let $\hc_k(G)$ denote its $k$th discrete singular cubical homology group. Suppose $n\geq 2$ and $A_k(G)$ is trivial for every $k<n$. **Discrete Hurewicz conjecture.** Then

$$
A_n(G)\cong \hc_n(G).
$$
 This is the proposed higher-dimensional analogue of the discrete Hurewicz theorem known in dimension $1$; the paper establishes the dimension-$1$ result and leaves this higher-dimensional statement conjectural.

345825.title: Conjecture on invariant extensions and regularity of edge-ideal powers
345825.statement:
Let $G$ and $G'$ be gap-free graphs. An **$(\operatorname{im},\reg)$-invariant extension** is a graph $G'$ obtained from $G$ by adding one new vertex, restricting to $G$ on the original vertices, and satisfying $\operatorname{im}(G')=\operatorname{im}(G)$ and $\reg(I(G'))=\reg(I(G))$.

**Invariant-extension conjecture.** If $\reg(I(G)^k)=2k$ for all $k\geq 2$, then $\reg(I(G')^k)=2k$ for all $k\geq 2$.

The conjecture is presented as a consequence of the Nevo–Peeva conjecture and is part of the paper's proposed approach to regularity of powers. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

345833.title: Schur-positivity conjecture for the decomposition poset
345833.statement:
Let $clambdain P^+$, let

$$
cmathcal{P}_{clambda}=cleft\{(clambda_1,clambda_2)in P^+\times P^+:clambda_1+clambda_2=clambdaright\},
$$

and order this set by $(clambda_1,clambda_2)succeq(cmu_1,cmu_2)$ exactly when $(clambda_1-clambda_2)(h_calpha)leq(cmu_1-cmu_2)(h_calpha)$ for every positive root $calpha$. Write $s_clambda$ for the Schur polynomial or character of $V(clambda)$. **Schur-positivity conjecture.** If $(clambda_1,clambda_2)succeq(cmu_1,cmu_2)$, then $s_clambda_1s_clambda_2-s_cmu_1s_cmu_2$ is Schur positive. The source states that this conjecture was proved by Loktev, Papi, and Ponomarev, so it is solved.

345906.title: Vanishing of the kernel for the ninth weak shuffle product
345906.statement:
Let $\underset{9}{\Box}$ be the weak shuffle product defined by $C_{9}$. For positive integers $p$ and $n$, let $K_{(n,p)}$ denote the kernel defined in the paper. **Vanishing-kernel conjecture.** For every positive integers $p$ and $n$, one has

$$
K_{(n,p)}=\{0\}.
$$

The claim concerns the kernel associated with powers in the ninth weak shuffle algebra. The supplied excerpt verifies the claim in low degrees $n=1,2,3$, but gives no general proof or resolution.

345919.title: The natural orientation conjecture for finite graphs
345919.statement: A finite graph $\Gamma$ is called **naturally oriented** if $H^1(\Gamma)$ has a basis whose supports are isomorphic, in the orientation-preserving sense, to cycles whose edges all point in the same direction; these supports are called **primitive cycles**. **Natural orientation conjecture.** Every finite graph has a natural orientation. Natural orientations would provide cohomology bases represented by edge forms with only $0$ and $1$ entries, giving a canonical combinatorial structure relevant to the action of the automorphism group on graph cohomology and to quantum mechanics on graphs. The source provides no resolution of the conjecture.

346036.title: Doubly connected graphs with arbitrarily close hot spots conjecture
346036.statement:
Let $epsilon>0$. A doubly connected metric graph is a graph of the type specified in the paper's location discussion. Let $\operatorname{diam}gamma$ denote its diameter, $\mu_2(gamma)$ its second eigenvalue, and $M$ its hot-spot set.

**Close hot-spots conjecture.** For every $epsilon>0$, there exists a doubly connected graph $gamma$ such that

$$
\operatorname{diam}gamma=1,
$$

$mu_2(gamma)$ is simple, and

$$
{\text{\rm max}}\{\operatorname{dist}(x,y):x,y\in M\}<epsilon.
$$

This shows that even without a tree-like boundary structure, the hot spots may be arbitrarily close relative to the graph diameter. The source gives no resolution status.

346180.title: Output-polynomial enumeration for incomparability graphs of $S_t$-free posets
346180.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer. A poset is **$S_t$-free** if it contains no suborder isomorphic to the poset $S_t$, and let $\textsc{Dom-Enum}$ denote the problem of enumerating all minimal dominating sets of a graph.

**The $S_t$-free incomparability conjecture.** For every $t$, there is an output-polynomial time algorithm for $\textsc{Dom-Enum}$ in incomparability graphs of $S_t$-free posets.

The result would extend the paper's bounded-dimension algorithm to a broader class of posets. The proposed extension is not covered by the current proof, which relies crucially on a bounded-dimension representation; the conjecture remains open.

346181.title: Output-polynomial enumeration for $2K_p$-free incomparability graphs
346181.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer, let $2K_p$ be the disjoint union of two copies of the clique $K_p$, and let $\textsc{Dom-Enum}$ denote the problem of enumerating all minimal dominating sets of a graph.

**The $2K_p$-free incomparability conjecture.** For every $p$, there is an output-polynomial time algorithm for $\textsc{Dom-Enum}$ in $2K_p$-free incomparability graphs.

This is presented as a directly easier conjecture than the corresponding statement for incomparability graphs of $S_t$-free posets. It holds for $p=1$ and is known for $p=2$, while the case $p=3$ is widely open without the incomparability assumption.

346182.title: Output-polynomial enumeration for $H$-free incomparability graphs
346182.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph. It is **co-bipartite** if its vertex set can be partitioned into two cliques, and let $\textsc{Dom-Enum}$ denote the problem of enumerating all minimal dominating sets of a graph.

**The co-bipartite forbidden-subgraph conjecture.** For any co-bipartite $H$, there is an output-polynomial time algorithm for $\textsc{Dom-Enum}$ in $H$-free incomparability graphs.

This is described as a bold generalization of the preceding conjecture. The case $H=C_4$ is known for incomparability graphs because $C_4$-free incomparability graphs are interval graphs, but the conjecture for arbitrary co-bipartite $H$ remains open.

346335.title: Căldăraru's conjecture for the ribbon graph complex in genera at least two
346335.statement:
Let $\mathsf{RGC}^g$ be the genus-$g$ part of the ribbon graph complex, with altered differential $\delta+\Delta$, where $\Delta$ is the Bridgeland differential, and let ${\rM}_g$ be the moduli space of curves of genus $g$ without marked points.

**Căldăraru's conjecture.** For every genus $g\geq 2$, there is a natural identification

$$
H(\mathsf{RGC}^{g},\delta+\Delta)\cong H_c({\rM}_g)[-1].
$$

This conjecture is presented as a consequence of the proposed comparison between the twisted hairy graph complex and the ribbon graph complex. The source gives no resolution status.

346736.title: Uniform size-bound conjecture for irreducible solutions of $(E_N)$
346736.statement:
Let $N$ be an integer greater than $2$, and let the **size** of an irreducible solution of $(E_N)$ mean the size notion defined earlier in the paper. **Uniform size-bound conjecture.** There exists a strictly positive integer $K$ such that, for every integer $N>2$, all irreducible solutions of $(E_N)$ have size less than $N+K$.

This is the second conjecture arising from the cases treated in the preceding section. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been proved or disproved.

346742.title: Hopkins–Rubey cyclic sieving conjecture for linear extensions of V(n)
346742.statement:
Let $V(n)$ be the poset in the source, let $\mathcal{L}(V(n))$ denote its set of linear extensions, and let $\operatorname{Pro}$ denote promotion. **Hopkins–Rubey's conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$, the rational expression

$$
f(q)=\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{3n}(1-q^{2i})}{\prod_{i=2}^{2n+1}(1-q^i)\prod_{i=2}^{n+1}(1-q^{2i})}
$$

is in $\mathbb{N}[q]$, and $(\mathcal{L}(V(n)),\langle\operatorname{Pro}\rangle,f(q))$ exhibits cyclic sieving.

The conjecture concerns both polynomiality with nonnegative coefficients and the orbit structure of promotion; the source does not report a resolution.

347085.title: Lescure–Meyniel and Abu-Khzam–Langston immersion coloring conjecture
347085.statement: Let $t$ be a positive integer. For a graph $H$, an **$H$-immersion** is a graph isomorphic to a graph obtained from a subgraph by repeatedly splitting off pairs of edges with a common end and deleting isolated vertices. A graph is properly $t$-colorable if its vertices can be partitioned into $t$ edgeless induced subgraphs. **Immersion coloring conjecture.** For every positive integer $t$, every graph with no $K_{t+1}$-immersion is properly $t$-colorable. This is the immersion analogue of Hadwiger's conjecture, independently proposed by Lescure and Meyniel and by Abu-Khzam and Langston; the source presents it as an open problem.

347256.title: Kloster–Král–Sullivan rational subgraph-regularity conjecture
347256.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph. It is walk-regular if $[A^r]_{ii}=[A^r]_{jj}$ for all vertices $i,j$ and every positive integer $r$, and it is $\beta$-subgraph regular if $[e^{\beta A}]_{ii}=[e^{\beta A}]_{jj}$ for all vertices $i,j$. **Kloster–Král–Sullivan conjecture.** The graph $\mathcal{G}$ is walk-regular if and only if there exists a rational number $\beta>0$ such that $\mathcal{G}$ is $\beta$-subgraph regular. The paper presents this as the rational-parameter refinement after the unrestricted single-parameter assertion was disproved.

347303.title: The wheel-graph adjacency-polytope volume conjecture
347303.statement:
Let $W_N=K_1\vee C_N$ be the wheel graph obtained by joining a single vertex to the cycle $C_N$, and let $\operatorname{NVol}(\nabla^{\operatorname{PQ}}_{W_N})$ denote the normalized volume of its type-PQ adjacency polytope. **Wheel-graph volume conjecture.** For all $N\geq 3$,

$$
\operatorname{NVol}(\nabla^{\operatorname{PQ}}_{W_N})=3^N-2^N+1.
$$

This gives a conjectural closed formula for the normalized volumes of wheel graphs, a planar class that is not generally outerplanar. The source provides no proof or resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

347368.title: Chow–Fan–Goemans–Vondrák wideness conjecture for Latin tableaux
347368.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition, and let a **Latin tableau** of shape $\lambda$ be a filling of the Young diagram of shape $\lambda$ such that row $i$ contains the numbers in $[\lambda_i]$ in some order and no number appears more than once in a column. A Young diagram $\lambda$ is called **wide** when it satisfies the wideness condition defined in the paper.

**Chow–Fan–Goemans–Vondrák conjecture.** A Young diagram $\lambda$ is wide if and only if there exists a Latin tableau of shape $\lambda$.

Latin tableaux generalize Latin squares and rectangles to arbitrary partition shapes. Wideness is necessary for the existence of a Latin tableau, while sufficiency remains open.

347573.title: Babai–Goodman bounded-orbit conjecture for automorphism groups of lattices
347573.statement:
A finite group $G$ is **realized** by a lattice $L$ if $\operatorname{Aut}(L)\simeq G$. An **orbit** means an orbit of the action of $\operatorname{Aut}(L)$ on the elements of $L$. **Babai–Goodman conjecture.** There exists a constant $k$ such that for any finite group $G$ there is a lattice $L$ realizing $G$ with at most $k$ orbits.

This conjecture asks whether the number of element orbits can be bounded independently of the finite group. Although every finite group can be realized by a lattice with a number of elements linear in $|G|$, the cited context notes that the number of edge orbits in graph realizations is not bounded; the boundedness of lattice-element orbits remains open.

347738.title: The universal fertility conjecture for consecutive-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting maps
347738.statement:
Let $S_3$ be the set of permutations of length $3$, and let $\operatorname{SC}_\sigma$ be the consecutive-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map associated with $\sigma$.

**Universal fertility conjecture.** For every $\sigma\in S_3$ and every positive integer $f$, there exists a permutation $\pi$ such that

$$
|\operatorname{SC}_\sigma^{-1}(\pi)|=f.
$$

This contrasts with the classical stack-sorting map, which has known infertility numbers. The assertion remains open for the consecutive-pattern-avoiding maps.

347807.title: Conlon's conjecture on the extremal number of fixed-length tight cycles
347807.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$ and let $C^{(r)}_{\ell}$ denote the $r$-uniform tight cycle of length $\ell$. **Conlon's conjecture.** There exists $c=c(r)>0$ such that, for every $\ell\geq r+1$ divisible by $r$, 

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,C^{(r)}_{\ell})=O\left(n^{r-1+\frac{c}{\ell}}\right).
$$

This is a conjecture about the extremal number of tight cycles of each fixed admissible length. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

348030.title: Grytczuk et al.'s finiteness conjecture for extremal pattern-avoiding words
348030.statement:
Let $P$ be an avoidable pattern, meaning that some alphabet admits arbitrarily long words avoiding $P$. For a fixed alphabet, an **extremal $P$-avoiding word** is a word that avoids $P$, but every extension obtained by inserting one letter contains $P$. **Grytczuk et al.'s finiteness conjecture.** For every avoidable pattern $P$, there exists a constant $k(P)$ such that the set of extremal $P$-avoiding words over a $k(P)$-letter alphabet is finite.

This conjecture proposes a finite extremal analogue of the theory of avoidable patterns. The paper uses it as motivation for studying extremal words for several other pattern classes; its resolution is not given here.
